title: MedEvoEval: Evaluating Continual Evolution of Doctor Agents through Simulated Clinical Episodes
claim: A benchmark composes role-specific agents, event logging, memory write-back and cross-episode analyses, unlike static fixed-input evaluations that only score final answers.
layout: Top comparison table, then panel A flow diagram, panel B timeline below
description: The figure stacks three parts. At the top is a plain comparison table with rows for information access, action validity, resource use, memory effects, stability and auditability. It contrasts fixed-input QA with MedEvoEval. Panel A, "Within-episode execution", is a boxed flow diagram. A structured medical case folder splits into PatientView, ExamView and ManagerView. Cartoon icons show a patient, an examination service, an optional MDT group, a central Doctor Agent and a manager scorer. Labeled arrows (ASK, REQUEST_TEST, CALL_MDT, FINALIZE) connect them. On the right, a dashed box holds event logs with process metrics and a memory write-back database. A dashed return arrow labeled top-K rule retrieval feeds back to the doctor agent. Panel B, "Cross-episode evaluation", is a purple timeline from Episode 1 to Episode T. Four labeled analyses sit above it: improvement, held-out transfer, update response and backward degradation. Blue and purple palettes distinguish the two panels.
caption: Overview of MedEvoEval. (A) Structured cases are split into patient, examination, and manager views. Doctor agents acquire evidence through inquiry and examination, optionally consult an MDT advisor, and submit final clinical outputs for manager scoring. Event logs record actions, observations, outputs, and scores, supporting process-cost measurement and optional experience write-back with top-$K$ rule retrieval for later episodes. (B) The resulting episode records support analyses of improvement, held-out transfer, update response, and backward degradation.
abstract: Doctor agents are moving beyond single-turn answer generation toward evolving clinical decision systems that acquire evidence within episodes and reuse experience across episodes. Fixed-input medical QA and many interactive benchmarks provide limited support for evaluating how episode-level decisions interact with cross-episode experience. We introduce MedEvoEval, an executable longitudinal evaluation framework based on action-gated simulated outpatient episodes. Each case is converted into role-specific patient, examination, and manager views; evidence is revealed through valid actions, and structured traces link observations, actions, final outputs, scores, and optional experience write-back. Experiments show that these traces expose process costs hidden by final-answer scoring, characterize how MDT-style consultation reallocates resources, and support analyses of memory maturation, held-out transfer, update-stage response, and backward retention. On 200 held-out cases, the mature-memory condition with sequential write-back reduces interaction turns by 0.915 and improves composite utility by 0.0483 after Holm correction. MedEvoEval provides a concrete basis for evaluating experience-driven improvement, transfer, and retention. The accompanying artifact provides 700 processed episode records with provenance, role-specific schemas, and execution, scoring, and analysis code.
